alex: Heads-up: I want to bump runtime config `fast_route_sampling` from 0.01 -> 0.10 for a few hours to collect telemetry on routing churn and cost impact. Before I do it I want to make sure the rollout has the usual telemetry gating + dry-run and an approver.

maya: Do we have the SLO guardrails we can tie this to? I want a clear metric to auto-rollback if p50 latency or serving error-rate changes.

simon: Suggestion: use the config API dry-run mode first to surface any schema/validation issues, then a probe that mirrors production traffic for 10m. Example curl for dry-run:

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/configs/apply?dry_run=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"key":"fast_route_sampling","value":0.10,"reason":"telemetry probe"}'
```

simon: Dry-run returns a plan with estimated affected routes and a sampling preview. We should log that plan to the rollout ticket.

rebecca: Console UX note: we should expose a "Preview with telemetry" toggle that annotates the change with the dry-run plan and required approver. Otherwise people flip flags blind. Can add a small banner: "This change will affect ~X routes".

carter: Ops ask: add a temporary telemetry alert and a trace-correlation tag for this probe so we can filter. Proposed temporary alert:
- trigger if p50 latency delta > 10% OR error-rate delta > 0.5% over baseline window (5m)

carter: Query we can pin in dashboards (Datadog example):
```
avg(last_5m): (p50_latency{env:prod,route:fast_route} - baseline_p50) / baseline_p50 > 0.10
```

config-bot: policy-check: rollout requires at least one approver from team "eng-platform" and an ops-slo guard.

alex: OK — proposed minimal rollout plan:
1) dry-run via API (simon) -> capture plan JSON into ticket
2) create temporary telemetry alert (carter) and enable trace tag `probe=fast_route_10pct`
3) console preview + approver (rebecca) -> require @maya approval
4) 10 minute probe on 10% sampling; monitor p50 and error-rate; auto-revert if gates hit

alex: I'll kick off step 1 after we confirm approver and alert.

maya: Approve pending that alert and that we add a short post-mortem template for the probe. :thumbsup:

simon: I'll run the dry-run now and paste the plan in the ticket.

rebecca: I'll add the preview toggle (small UX patch) and wire the approver flow to require a checkbox for "Telemetry gating present".

carter: I'll add the temporary alert and a small runbook snippet to the ticket for on-call (how to revert config via API).

alex: Awesome — thanks all. I'll set a 30m window on calendar to watch results. Will post probe start/stop in this thread.

simon: dry-run done, plan JSON attached to ticket #PLAT-492 (no schema errors).

config-bot: deploy-check: preview-UX patch CI passed.

alex: Starting probe in ~10m with `fast_route_sampling=0.10` for 10m. If alert fires we'll revert immediately.

carter: Alert created and linked to PLAT-492. Playbook updated.

maya: Confirmed approver check done. Good to go.

simon: Probe started. I'll stream a quick log snippet to the ticket.

(replies and short updates over the 10m probe)

carter: No alert so far at +6m. p50 delta ~2%. error-rate delta ~0.05%.

alex: Probe finished, no automatic rollback triggered. I'll leave the config at 10% for another hour for extra samples, then scale back to 1% and collect final metrics.

rebecca: Filed small UX follow-up to show sample-estimate next to toggle.

alex: Thanks everyone. Outcome: probe ok, no rollback. Next: collect results and publish short post-mortem and cost delta.

rebecca: I'll put the UX PR + screenshots in PLAT-492.

simon: I'll attach the probe trace set and p50/error graphs to the ticket.

alex: Closing this thread for now — will reopen if we see regressions. ✅
